title: Examination and Supervisory Privilege Parity Act of 2014
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on July 29, 2014. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Examination and Supervisory Privilege Parity Act of 2014 - Amends the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010, with respect to the supervision of nondepository covered persons, to include state agencies that licence, supervise, or examine the offering of consumer financial products or services among the regulatory agencies with which the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) is required to coordinate its supervisory activities.

Declares that the sharing of information with such regulators, authorities, and agencies shall not be construed as waiving, destroying, or otherwise affecting any privilege or confidentiality claimed by nondepository covered persons under federal or state law regarding such information as to any person or entity other than the CFPB, agency, supervisor, or authority.

summary.headline: This 2014 law lets the CFPB share supervision information with state agencies that oversee consumer financial products without losing legal privileges held by nonbank companies.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010 so that state agencies which license, supervise, or examine consumer financial products or services are part of the group the CFPB must coordinate with on supervision of nonbank companies. It also says that sharing information with these agencies does not waive or erase any privilege or confidentiality a nonbank company claims under federal or state law. That protection applies to everyone except the CFPB and the agency or authority receiving the information.

who_it_affects.group: Nonbank companies that offer consumer financial products or services
who_it_affects.how: Information they share with the CFPB or with state regulators during supervision keeps its legal privilege or confidentiality protection as against other parties.

who_it_affects.group: State agencies that license, supervise, or examine consumer financial products
who_it_affects.how: They are added to the list of agencies that the CFPB must coordinate its supervisory work with on nonbank companies.
It must include these state agencies in its coordination of supervisory activities.
